Decision (Jason, 2026-10-20, DR-20): an external client needs mcp.verdify.ai. Keep the public route, put a Cloudflare Access service-token gate in front of it, give that client its own MCP audience token, and rotate the Iris token. Removing the route is declined.

Acceptance: the body's four criteria stand, plus: the external client authenticates with its own audience token and the Access service token, and the old Iris token value is rejected.

Jason's follow-up on DR-20 (2026-10-20): identify the external client **from the mcp.verdify.ai access logs**, then confirm it with Jason before issuing its service token. Edge work is on the network lane's Cloudflare Access issue.

1002.body:
Decision (Jason, 2026-10-19): **graphs.verdify.ai stays public.** It serves the graphs for the public site lab.verdify.ai, so turning off anonymous access is not the fix. Rescoped goal: keep the public graphs, but stop anonymous users from running arbitrary SQL through `/api/ds/query`. Options, in order of preference:
1. Serve lab.verdify.ai panels through Grafana **public dashboards** (shared links render only the saved panel queries), and turn off anonymous Viewer org access.
2. If anonymous Viewer must stay, point the public org at a datasource that uses a DB role limited to curated views (a read-only role with only SELECT on the public views, `statement_timeout`, and no other tables or functions), and apply Grafana datasource permissions so anonymous users can query only that datasource.
3. Add a rate limit or WAF rule on `/api/ds/query` at the edge as defence in depth.

Acceptance: lab.verdify.ai graphs render for anonymous visitors, and an anonymous `POST /api/ds/query` with arbitrary rawSql returns 401/403, or can read only the curated public views under a statement timeout.

## Carry-over from #786, #787 and #379 (consolidated 2026-10-20)

Jason approved this consolidation on 2026-10-20. Three follow-on decisions closed as not planned, because each one was only a go/no-go to record at this readout. This issue already requires an explicit stop, repair, retest or follow-on decision. The following clauses are added to its acceptance, and `planning/backlog.yaml` carries the same text.

- [ ] **Comparator (from #786):** record an explicit go/no-go. If go, use a fixed numeric rule and a genuine chronological held-out corpus. Offline command replay supports no revealed-schedule tuning and no physical claim. Any new trial gets its own identity, lock, draw and measured claim. The PR #932 preparation (efaa4b67, artifact SHA256 `dedaecdc…`) stays the reference.
- [ ] **Resource study (from #787):** record an explicit go/no-go on a measured heating, overnight or resource study.
  - #410 (overnight evidence) and #981 (electricity) are inputs to this decision, not blockers. Their native edges to #787 are removed.
  - Every claimed resource needs independent, eligible, calibrated coverage and uncertainty. Stale or modeled values stay labeled.
  - If go, the study is a prospective season or overnight design with a bounded measured claim that can test climate improvement and resource benefit as stated, or the claim is explicitly narrowed.
  - No yield, profit or whole-resource claim, hardware purchase, gas tuning or seasonal controller expansion follows automatically from the current pilot or without a separate decision.
  - Specification e52284cf stays the reference.
- [ ] **Response model or MPC (from #379):** a grey-box or MPC path is proposed only after held-out calibration and response gates pass against persistence and simpler baselines.
  - No PID treatment arm or new outer-loop control enters the current experiment.
  - Any justified controller change gets a separately reviewed, bounded implementation and release plan.
  - The history of two failed closed-loop models and the open-loop PID result (64–138% more runtime on the factual trajectory) stays linked as evidence.

The #379→#786→#785 blocking chain is removed, and these decisions now end here. #378's edge from this issue is unchanged.
